events.content:
The PPR shell for `/` now prerenders the full page layout with per-section skeletons instead of a bare spinner. `next build` confirms the route as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` with the static HTML containing `
`, `

Dashboard

`, and three independent streaming boundaries. **What was wrong** `page.tsx` did `await getDashboardData()` at the top and passed the results down as props. With `cacheComponents: true`, that uncached `fetch` made the *entire* page dynamic, so the only thing Next could put in the static shell was the `loading.tsx` fallback. Users saw a spinner and then the whole dashboard appeared at once, gated on the slowest data. **What I changed** - `app/data.ts` (new): moved `getDashboardData` here and wrapped it in React's `cache()` so the three sections share a single fetch per request while still suspending independently. - `app/CardStats.tsx`, `app/RevenueChart.tsx`, `app/LatestInvoices.tsx`: each is now an async server component that reads its own slice of the data, and each exports a matching `*Skeleton` component with the same structure (headings, list shape) so the layout doesn't shift when content arrives. - `app/page.tsx`: now a synchronous component with no data access. It renders the heading and wraps each section in its own `` with its skeleton as the fallback. The result is that the shell (layout, heading, section headings, skeletons) is served instantly from the static prerender, and each of the three sections streams in as soon as its data resolves, rather than everything waiting on one top-level await. Two notes: `loading.tsx` is now effectively unused for this route, since the page no longer suspends at the top level; I left it in place as a harmless fallback rather than widen the change. The skeletons use a `skeleton` class, but there's no stylesheet in this project — the existing `card`/`chart`/`spinner` classes are also unstyled, so I followed that convention rather than introducing CSS.
